what_lands: The fourth of the fourteen. charged_strike/receipt_walk retires in Amendment L, Ruling 1's whole shape: the family's thirteen mechanics all declare, the eleven that author a damage row declare both halves (eleven ViewTag.THEORETICAL pair previews and eleven APPLIED walk halves delivered as HolderPacket, PER_HOLDER, PAIRED), the five engine sites that author those rows stamp pair_preview_of and hand the walk an AuthoredDeclaration per event under them, interpreters.charged_strike.WALK_INTERPRETER registers at (CHARGED_STRIKE, RECEIPT_WALK), and survival.transitions.apply_declared_price prices each declaration at the resistance that packet met. The deferral row leaves docs/behavior-frontier.json in the same commit with the reason its surviving compiled-lane twin can no longer share corrected there (R-36).
why_this_family_is_startable_now: Its two prerequisites are both discharged and both are measured rather than asserted. Umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 2's source-derived term census is green -- 29 post-authoring packet-mutation sites, 0 uncovered -- which is the standing precondition on retiring any further family, and Ruling 3's window-armed covering scenario is this family's own: lethality_window_assassin_roster arms a Voltaic Cyclosword Firmament window, and Firmament IS one of this family's eleven strikes. The window that stopped the first active_cast attempt is therefore inside this slice's enumerated population rather than outside every baseline, on the one packet whose own window re-prices it.

landed_against.rule: R-17/R-32/D-97 -- no baseline moves inside any semantic commit of this slice. The code lands against the committed baselines plus this allowlist; a re-capture, if the measurement ever asks for one, is the integration agent's own commit.

qualifying_population.rule: R-20's second half. The count is not readable off the pre-change tree by inspection: this slice moves where a number comes from rather than editing a formula, so which leaves can move is a property of which participants hold a declaring owner of the family, and that is a fact about the committed scenario set rather than about the diff. The population is therefore enumerated from committed artifacts -- the committed docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json at f9d2817, whose own fields are derived from the behaviour catalog and from scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json's scenario subtrees -- before the slice's first src/ edit. Any occurrence outside it is an unexpected one and stops the slice exactly as an over-count would.
qualifying_population.predicate: Every committed coupled scenario that puts a declaring owner of the charged_strike family on a participant. The thirteen owners are read live from the behaviour catalog over rule_owners() -- Bastionbreaker, Dead Man's Plate, Fiendhunter Bolts, Guinsoo's Rageblade, Heartsteel, Hullbreaker, Kraken Slayer, Rapid Firecannon, Statikk Shiv, Stormrazor, Umbral Glaive, Voltaic Cyclosword, Yun Tal Wildarrows -- which is the same family-to-owner join golden_snapshot.receipt_walk_families() makes for the coverage guard, so the population and the guard cannot disagree about which rosters can see the family.
qualifying_population.method: scripts.receipt_walk_schedule.population_size over each selected scenario subtree of the committed coupled baseline -- the same instrument, and the same conservative bound, the retirement schedule uses for the remaining rows: the whole scenario subtree, because a slice that moves a family's pricing can move any aggregate downstream of it inside that scenario.
qualifying_population.why_this_population_can_see_what_the_sli: Two scenarios and both of them are load-bearing rather than a count. crit_onhit_carry_roster puts Kraken Slayer on a Caitlyn attacking two enemies at full uptime, which is this family's repeating-strike shape -- four procs per fight, each re-read against the target's falling health, so the per-proc magnitudes differ from each other and a declaration that split one row total evenly would price the walk's packets at a number no proc had. lethality_window_assassin_roster puts Voltaic Cyclosword on a Zed, which is the empowered-hit shape AND the one packet in the fourteen families whose own temporary-lethality window re-prices it: Firmament grants its lethality before its own packet, so _apply_temporary_lethality_windows restates this declaration's resistance and the walk prices it at what the packet met rather than at the fight's published 68.0 armour (Amendment N, Ruling 1).

pair_engine_population.why: scripts/golden_baseline.json is the one-attacker pair-engine surface, and this slice adds no pair-engine arithmetic: the two stamps it adds pair-side -- pair_preview_of on each strike row and the row's own declaration on the events under it -- are not leaves that baseline holds, which records each build's sorted breakdown_keys and its total_damage and neither a row's inner fields nor an event. Zero pair-engine golden diffs is therefore a declared population of zero rather than an observation, and a single diff there stops the slice.

qualifying_population.predicted: 0 occurrences inside a population of 4882. The walk's from-declaration price and the pair engine's are the same real number with the multiplications associated differently -- the pair engine mitigates and then applies the holder's amps, the walk composes the amps pre-mitigation and mitigates once (Amendment M, Ruling 1) -- so the two agree to within one unit in the last place, four orders of magnitude below the 0.005 golden equality grades to (R-13). The resistance each side prices at is the same one under Amendment N, Ruling 1. A leaf that did move could only move by 0.01, which qualifies under none of R-15's three tests.

what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.why_it_is_written_down_in_advance: This family is not one authoring site and not one arithmetic. A charge is spent by an attack, by an ability, by an ultimate's empowered run or by every Nth on-hit application, and the engine times each of those in a different place -- so what a declaration owes is enumerated here before the edit rather than discovered by whichever total came out short (Amendment M, Ruling 1's second forbidden shape, a deletion wearing a re-spelling's name).
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_per_packet_magnitude: Per packet and never a row total split evenly. A repeating strike (Kraken Slayer, Hullbreaker) re-reads the target's falling health per proc, and an energized strike re-reads it per proc too, so the raws differ within one row. The on-hit effectiveness of the application that spent the charge is folded in, because it is a pair-local allocation of one application rather than an amplifier.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_target_side_basic_multiplier: Folded into the magnitude wherever the engine applies it -- source.basic_damage and a non-true class -- because the engine multiplies it AFTER mitigation and the pricing stage has no term for it. Mitigation is linear, so one folded magnitude prices to the same real number; leaving it out would delete a target-side factor from every total that holds one.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_attack_class: AttackClass.OTHER for four of the five sites, and it is measured rather than defaulted: an item's own charged packet is priced by damage._mitigate and by nothing else, so no part amp is owed. The fifth is the exception and states it -- damage._simulate_auto_attacks multiplies Fiendhunter Bolts' true instance by the holder's BASIC part amp because that instance rides the swing itself -- so that one declares AttackClass.BASIC_ATTACK and lets StaticHolderAmps.factor_for deliver the amp, pre-mitigation, instead of pre-multiplying the magnitude.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_resistance: Absent at authoring, which is the correct reading for a packet that met the fight's published figure, and restated by damage._restate_declaration at every site that re-prices the packet afterwards (Amendment N, Ruling 1). This family owns the window that does it: Voltaic Cyclosword's Firmament is one of its own strikes, and it re-prices its own packet.
what_a_declaration_of_this_family_has_to.the_coarse_row: Two of the five sites can author a row with no events of its own -- an energized strike whose procs landed on no timestamped swing, and a repeating strike holding an ability-segment proc, which stays coarse deliberately. Those rows state the declaration once at row level and damage._row_declaration_share splits it the way the reconstruction splits the damage, so a row that fell into two damage types cannot hand one magnitude to two packets.

why_two_of_the_thirteen_mechanics_are_no.rule: Amendment L, Ruling 1 requires a retiring family's pair rows to be stamped pair_preview_of and declared THEORETICAL. It says nothing about a mechanic that authors no row, and this is the first of the fourteen families that has one.
why_two_of_the_thirteen_mechanics_are_no.measured: guinsoos_rageblade.swing_rate and yun_tal_wildarrows.swing_rate are SwingScheduleRule payloads. Measured on a fight holding each owner alone, neither authors a breakdown row: a schedule changes how often the holder swings, which the pair engine applies while building the swing stream every later site reads. There is no packet, so there is nothing for a walk to price and nothing for a preview to double-count.
why_two_of_the_thirteen_mechanics_are_no.consequence: Both are declared -- required fields, no defaults -- as APPLIED pair halves with PAIR_ONLY authority, which is the statement 'this mechanic's pair-lane number is delivered and previewed by nobody'. Declaring them as THEORETICAL previews would be a false claim about a row that does not exist; leaving them undeclared would be the omission D-40 forbids. tests/test_survival_kernel.py::TestTheOptInSetIsExactlyTheFamiliesThatRetired::test_no_family_is_half_retired reads that difference off the declaration rather than off a list of names, so an undeclared rule of a re-priced family fails there.
why_two_of_the_thirteen_mechanics_are_no.what_keeps_it_honest: D-62's uniqueness is asserted on the family that did retire, not assumed for the two that had nothing to retire: no leaf sums a pair-authored preview and the walk's price, measured per family by the two parametrised cases in tests/test_survival_kernel.py, which now run for charged_strike because the family is read off the declarations.

no_baseline_moves: R-32's five baselines are untouched by every commit of this slice. docs/behavior-frontier.json and docs/receipts/receipt-walk-retirement-schedule.json are machine-derived receipts whose counters this slice moves, so they move with it (R-36); holding them back would make the slice red against a gate it is forbidden to contain.

measured_after.golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. The declared pair-engine population of 0 held.
measured_after.coupled_golden: python scripts/golden_snapshot.py compare scripts/golden_coupled_baseline.json -- OK: snapshot identical. Zero of the 4882 enumerated leaves moved.
measured_after.oracle_receipts_owed: None. R-19 owes an investigator per qualifying occurrence (R-15) and there were none, in a population enumerated in advance and non-empty.
measured_after.what_the_walk_actually_priced: A zero on a baseline is evidence a family's numbers did not move; it is not evidence the walk priced anything. Read off survival.transitions.apply_declared_price itself over the two covering scenarios: the walk priced kraken_slayer.repeating_strike at 86.58782853380173 on on_hit_Kraken Slayer and voltaic_cyclosword.empowered_hit at 152.23529411764704 on on_hit_once_Voltaic Cyclosword_ability, one pricing per (source_key, rule), each equal to the declaration's own price re-computed from the resistances that packet met. The pair engine's own rows carry 86.58782853380173 and 152.23529411764707 for the same two packets, so the two engines agree to one unit in the last place -- four orders of magnitude below the 0.005 the golden equality grades to.
measured_after.the_window_case_is_the_one_that_matters: lethality_window_assassin_roster publishes an effective armour of 68.0 and the Firmament packet never meets it: Firmament's extra lethality applies to its own packet, so damage._apply_temporary_lethality_windows restates the declaration's resistance and the walk prices it at what the packet met. Pricing it at the published baseline instead would have been the deletion umbrella Amendment N, Ruling 1 forbids, on the exact packet the ruling was written for -- and it is this family's own strike, which is why this family is the first that could exercise the term end to end.
measured_after.the_gate_the_population_could_not_bound: R-01 row 8 is green on all four bench scenarios with and without the compiled walk, and mundo_3champ's winning build holds Voltaic Cyclosword and Bastionbreaker -- two of this family's owners, re-priced from their declarations inside a searched build -- with its score unchanged at 3305.0. That row is the one that saw the missing resistance term when no committed scenario could; it sees this family's re-pricing too, and it did not move.
